classification.difficultyReason: Read the shaded bounds from supplied graphs and directly integrate positive reciprocal expressions; part a also permits a simple intercept check.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the area of the region bounded by $y=3-\frac{3}{x}$, the $x$-axis and $x=3$.

spec.description: Increasing reciprocal curve with its bounded region shaded, horizontal guides at y=2 and y=3, and labelled boundary values.
spec.mathematics: y=3-3/x; intercept (1,0); endpoint (3,2); horizontal asymptote y=3; shaded region 1<=x<=3, 0<=y<=3-3/x.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph and shaded region remain visible in the student edition.

answer.worked:
The curve meets the $x$-axis when $3-\frac{3}{x}=0$, so $x=1$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\int_1^3\left(3-\frac{3}{x}\right)\,dx\\&=\left[3x-3\ln x\right]_1^3\\&=(9-3\ln 3)-3\\&=(6-3\ln 3)\,\text{u}^2.\end{align*}$$
